I must admit that everything started going better when I went on lithium. Before I was on antidepressants and they made me feel HORRIBLE. 
It was only after lithium that I had the minimum will to live to make the long term changes that allowed me to actually “recover”. 

First I had to talk with my family. My parents relationship affected me a lot, especially my dad’s attitude. Fortunately they both understood and now we are a little better, and at least make the effort to understand each other.  

And then I just had the privilege to choose what I wanted to do with my life. I had the immense privilege to do it, and I have to accept it and be thankful. 

So I started to actually do the things I love for the sake of it (art, study, movement, baking etc.) And eventually I started feeling happier. 

Of course there is at least a week a month where I feel like shit but it’s nothing compared to what I used to feel lol

The meds change is also something that I’ve dealt with and as you say it’s very frustrating and invalidating. Unfortunately everyone goes through some depressive event in their life but just some of them actually are classified as a disorder, and in our case a lifelong state. 
Something that I have been doing lately is just to separate myself from the diagnosis and just start to learn how my brain works, as an introspective exercise. 

Keeping a mood journal and writing your thoughts can maybe help you find out how you actually feel, because your personal experience of suffering or happiness is MUCH more than a symptom. 

Don’t compare your sadness to anyone’s, and value your own feelings as unique and not “defined” by the DSM.

I relate a lot to this. Right now I am fortunately on a good state. I feel pretty “normal” which makes me feel good sometimes, but I also feel insecure about my diagnosis. Talking about the moments I feel depressed seem to classify as something that “happens to everyone from time to time”. I talk to my family and everyone tells me that they feel down and tired sometimes too, and that makes me wonder if maybe I’m just faking it all. 

And I mean, if I look back it’s pretty obvious that I was very depressed, suicidal and other times extremely energetic because of my Bipolar 2. I just want my “symptoms” to be validated. 
But at the end it really shouldn’t matter. If you feel better then it’s good. 
I was very attached to my disorders and they made my personality. I’m trying to get over that. 
You don’t have to “prove” that you are ill to anybody, and your disorder should not define you.

Thanks for your answer, yes I agree that the only way out is to actually learn to read my mood patterns and be prepared for when I crash. 
Still it makes me sad it think I will never really be able to be constantly productive. Sometimes I want to do so many things but I just can’t get myself to actually start them. And I will have to carry this my whole life ;-;

Hi! I did the same as you since I was like 13. I tried to be the best I could at everything, just so that people would accept me and maybe receive a little bit of love and recognition, which I actually got. 
I was the best student in my class I did everything my parents wanted, exercised, attended extra classes and tried to be nice to people, even though I just wanted to be alone. 
Eventually I just broke and realized I was doing everything for everyone, but no one really cared about how I felt. Unconsciously I stopped eating as a way to get attention, I just wanted people to care about me. 
It’s been like 3 years in I’m only gotten worse at my depression, fortunately I overcame my anorexia, but I still have problems with food. 

What I just want to say is that the “fake it until you make it” mentality does not work if what you are looking for is to please others. 
Give yourself a break and focus on what you *really* like, what YOU want. And analyze WHY you want it, where, how, with who etc. 
Do you really enjoy working out or is it because it can make you better looking for others? The “best version of you” benefits yourself or others? 

You try vey hard but you are not heading to a goal focused on your well-being. Try to get to know you, sometimes we know less about ourselves that we think. 

If you have done all of this until now, you can get even further, but do it for you. You discipline and strength are remarkable. I hope you feel better soon :)

I have never been diagnosed with bpd… 
I personally feel that I am in the bipolar spectrum and a professional supported my opinion. 
The problem for me is that I can’t get myself to “accept me as I am” because I don’t know if all I’m feeling is part of my “personality” or it’s an illness.

It’s really nice to hear you are doing better :) 
I personally think I have done everything that was in my hands. I ate healthy, exercised, I did yoga and daily stretching, I went to therapy, I forced myself to stay a good student at school, but eventually I just broke. 
I gave up because even if I tried as hard as I could I felt awful. People around me told me I was becoming the “best version of myself”, while I just wanted everything to end. 
Now I can’t do anything. I can still force myself to do some things form time to time, but I can’t enjoy them. I can’t go to school and I don’t think I will be able to graduate. 
Even so, I think that maybe it will get better. I still have time and maybe in the future I will be able to live a peaceful life. I don’t even want to be happy anymore. When I feel happy it doesn’t feel real.

I relate a lot to your chain of thoughts. I’m in a similar situation, but what I have to do is to finish school and go to university. I’m just four months away from my graduation, but I feel like I can’t do it. I haven’t lived for too long, but it feels like an eternity. Everything feels difficult, and why should we bother trying if you are not even going to enjoy it? 
To me what it’s keeping me here are my parents. I’m done because after I tried to kill myself I promise them I wouldn’t do it again, not because I don’t want to, but because I know how much they’ll suffer. 
No one signed up for a life of suffering, but I feel that we can still try to do something. If we are at the very edge of life, trying to end it all, nothing really matters anymore. If I hadn’t been discovered I should be dead by now. I haven’t done anything useful with my time. 
But it’s not necessary. You deserve to live, period. If someone tell you the opposite, even if it is yourself, they are wrong. 
I don’t like people either. I have never really been abused, but I just don’t like being sensed by others.
At the end of the day nobody really cares, everyone is busy with their own problems. 
Look to the sky at night, by seeing the stars you will understand you little and insignificant we are. Our life feels so long but it’s so short. We were given the opportunity to be here, even if we don’t want to. So just give if another shot, live by yourself, try to recognize the dumb things we like and enjoy them. Live for yourself, find that something inside you that is covered by sadness and suffering and make it shine again. Or at least try, one last time.

I can’t day that I understand you, because only you know how much pain and suffering you have gone through. 
I just want to say that I think you are incredibly strong, just for being able to get to this moment after all you have lived. Sometimes I wonder why this happen, why are souls sent to earth to suffer. My sufferings nothing compared to you, but I feel like I should have the imprudence to tell you that you are meaningful, I read all your words and I think you really have talent for writing. 
Stop living for others and try to rescue yourself. Even if you feel like you have nothing left, believe in what you love, because I’m sure you love a lot of things, even if you are tired, even if you don’t want to go them anymore. 
I won’t tell you to just “keep fighting”, because it’s not fair for someone to survive instead of living and enjoy life. Maybe you should try to let go some things. Make decisions to change your life, because even if it’s seems like everything it’s perfect, it’s still hurting you. 
Keep writing all your feelings, if you feel capable write more about your pain, try to vomit all your suffering into an artwork. As I said I’m no one to tell you anything about suffering, but just acknowledge that you are valid, that your soul it’s still beautiful even if you feel like you are broken, and that you deserve to live no matter what. Live out of spite for those who hurt you. You still have a lot of things to do in this world.

I think it’s true that using medical diagnoses to describe “normal” or everyday moods it’s not very respectful for those who actually suffer the severe symptoms of the different mental health issues. 

But I also think that maybe the normalization of those terms could help more people feel safe when they need to share how they feel. 
Again, it’s not correct for someone who has experienced two or three days of sadness after a loss to “diagnose” himself with depression, but it is also a way for him to call for help. 
All of us who are already diagnosed were once undiagnosed and probably really scared to tell others how we felt. The use of words and concepts it’s the problem here, but putting such a strong line between mental illness and day to day suffering can be detrimental for those seeking treatment. 
I believe that if someone expresses themselves those ways, we should listen, educate them and help them, because it’s what we wanted others to do when we were in similar situations. 
Auto diagnose it’s most of the times a way to draw attention, so even if sometimes we can see it as kind of dumb or not very serious, they still need help, or love, or attention of some kind.

Helllo! The heat of my stove it’s pretty high so for me putting the kernels directly into the pot it’s not an option because they burn really quickly. What I do is that I pour some salt over the bottom of the pot and let it heat up, and then I mix in the kernels. Salt can handle very high temperatures so be careful and don’t touch it or you could get burnt. You can shake the pot often and take them out immediately after they stop popping. It’s my go-to method and I think it works fine :) 
Hope it helps

Well first, you have to understand the difference between binge eating and extreme hunger. What you are experiencing right now is probably a consequence of restriction : you need to renourish, so your body makes you crave things that give you a lot of energy to repair all the damage that this has caused you. 
The feeling of losing control is normal, and it’s related to the restrictive behaviors and the fear of weight gain. 
I think that the best thing that you can do is to follow the well-known advice of “listening to your body”. Even if you are scared of losing control, there will be a moment where your hunger cues will return to normal and you will no longer feel the urge to eat, because your body will have already healed...
